stem: A client with diabetic gastroparesis is prescribed metoclopramide. Which therapeutic effect should the nurse expect?

options.A: Increased upper gastrointestinal motility with accelerated gastric emptying.
options.C: Permanent blockade of gastric acid production.
options.D: Formation of a protective ulcer coating over the duodenum.

rationale: Metoclopramide stimulates motility of the upper gastrointestinal tract, increases antral contractions and small-intestinal peristalsis, and accelerates gastric emptying and intestinal transit. These prokinetic effects support its use in diabetic gastroparesis.
educational_objective: Explain the prokinetic effect of metoclopramide in diabetic gastroparesis.
source_locator: Clinical Pharmacology §12.1—stimulates upper-GI motility and accelerates gastric emptying
source_claim_supported: Metoclopramide increases upper-GI motility and accelerates gastric emptying.
correction_summary: Retained the useful mechanism but tied it to the current label and a clinical indication rather than an unsupported simplified mechanism.
audit_findings: Correct option is explicitly described in §12.1.
Other options describe opposite or unrelated GI drug effects.
Independent second pass found one best answer.
